authoredFrom: PS7/PS20/PS21/PS22 — the module surface: imports in, exports out. Authored 2026-09-26. PS7: the pre-wave import reader took the token after ANY `command_parameter` as the module's name, so `Import-Module Az.Accounts -ErrorAction Stop` stored TWO external module imports — `Az.Accounts` and `Stop`. PS20: `exports: []` was hard-coded, so a module's public API was invisible. PS21: `using` was listed in `FLOW_KEYWORDS`, which is where the pre-wave lane filtered it, so `using namespace System.IO` published nothing at all. PS22: only `#requires -Module` was read, so `#requires -Version 7.0` — the commonest form — published nothing. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING underneath all four: this grammar puts `command_argument_sep` BETWEEN a parameter and its value, so `command_elements` for `Import-Module -Name SqlServer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` is `[sep, command_parameter(-Name), sep, generic_token(SqlServer), sep, …]` and the value sits at i+3. Every `namedChild(i + 1)` read found a separator, so NO two-token parameter value was read anywhere in the language. A second gate was over-strict in the other direction: requiring a module argument to look like a PATH dropped every installed module, which is named bare (`Import-Module PoshRSJob`), while `Az.Accounts` survived only because a dot happens to match the extension regex.

forbidExports.name: Get-Internal
forbidExports.comment: PRE-FIX SHAPE: the module declared NO exports at all (`exports: []` was hard-coded), so a reader could not tell which of the two functions was public. FORBIDDING the private one is what makes the export surface a SURFACE — an export list naming everything would say nothing. (Two authoring errors here, both caught by the lane rather than by me: this entry was ALSO in `expectExports`, and both entries used the key `export`. The convention on these two channels is `name` — only `expectExportRanges` takes `export` — so a pin written the other way can never match. That second failure is what exposed a real harness defect alongside it: the two export matchers were hand-rolled every-field loops that did not skip the documentation fields, so a `comment` on a pin became a failing assertion. They now route through `matchConstraints` like every other channel.)
